extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and supervisors (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on when and how to reject patent claims, the substantive statutory grounds and procedural requirements for rejections, and the form and content of Office actions addressing rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (statutory grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define a useful, novel, nonobvious, and enabled invention that has been clearly described in the specification (requirements of 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standards of patentability applied in examination must be the same throughout the Office. All requirements for patentability (e.g., patent eligible, useful, novel, nonobvious, enabled, and clearly described as provided in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112) must be met before a claim is allowed. A claim should not be allowed merely because it recites in detail all features (a 'picture' claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard to be applied in all cases is the 'preponderance of the evidence' test: an examiner should reject a claim if, in view of the prior art and evidence of record, it is more likely than not that the claim is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This uniform standard applies regardless of art unit complexity or crowdedness; examiners must apply this burden when deciding to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early, clear articulation of rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of examination is to clearly articulate any rejection early in the prosecution process so that the applicant has the opportunity to provide evidence of patentability and otherwise reply completely at the earliest opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the application has been read and the claimed invention understood and a prior art search made, the examiner should review and analyze the application with the prior art and articulate rejections early; the examiner then reviews all evidence before issuing the next Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of best references and designation of relied parts
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command. When a reference is complex or shows inventions other than that claimed, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified. Language used in rejecting claims should be unequivocal (see MPEP § 707.07(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reliance on admissions and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) as to matters affecting patentability and, insofar as rejections in applications are concerned, may also rely upon facts within his or her knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the record can form the basis of a rejection in addition to cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of commonly owned or joint-research prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that would otherwise qualify as prior art may be treated as commonly owned or as subject to a joint research agreement (and thus excluded) if the applicant/patent owner provides appropriate statements and disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)/102(b)(2)(C) or pre‑AIA 102/103(c), an applicant may provide statements that subject matter and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or were made under a joint research agreement, and must disclose/identify the parties as required. Specific conditions and statements are set out for various statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive handling of form defects or missing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application discloses patentable subject matter but the claims in their present form cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s action should be constructive and when possible should offer a definite suggestion for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting patentable subject matter disclosed but not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates the applicant intends to claim such subject matter, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects or features have not been claimed and that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is advisory language the examiner may include to guide the applicant toward claiming patentable aspects disclosed in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after applicant reply (continued examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reply by applicant to a non-final action, the application will be reconsidered and again examined; applicant may reply with or without amendment unless the action is final, an appeal has been taken, or other specified closures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.112 governs reconsideration. Amendments after an appeal are subject to 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (c). Ex parte and inter partes reexamination procedures and limitations are noted; examiners must follow procedures on final vs non-final actions and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rejection (substance) and objection (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'rejection' is the refusal to grant claims because the subject matter as claimed is considered unpatentable; an 'objection' is made when the form of the claim (as distinguished from its substance) is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections are subject to review by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, while objections, if persisted, may be reviewed only by petition to the Director. Formal matters should not be combined in appeals to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based on prior art (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most frequent ground of rejection is unpatentability in view of the prior art — lack of novelty under 35 U.S.C. 102 or obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prior‑art rejections examiners should follow specific MPEP sections for choosing best art, handling foreign docs, determining effective filing dates, and preparing form paragraphs (many topics moved to MPEP § 2120 et seq., § 2132‑2156 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections not based on prior art must be fully developed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection not based on prior art is proper (e.g., lack of adequate written description, enablement, utility, subject matter eligibility, etc.), such rejection should be stated with a full development of the reasons rather than by a mere conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should review each claim for compliance with every statutory requirement during initial review. Deficiencies should be explained clearly and, whenever practicable, indicate how rejections may be overcome and how problems may be resolved. Relevant MPEP sections are cited for specific grounds (e.g., §§ 2104‑2107, 2161‑2174).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of previously allowed claims (procedural safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable may be rejected only after a primary examiner has considered all the facts; an Office action rejecting a previously allowed claim must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised. When assigned an application with prior actions by another examiner, the new examiner should review the previous search and generally should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely hoping to find something. Use Form Paragraph 7.50 to indicate prior allowance now withdrawn and cite newly discovered references; actions including this form paragraph require Primary Examiner signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of claims copied from a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims corresponding to claims of a patent are presented in an application, the examiner must determine whether the presented claims are unpatentable on any grounds (35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103, 112, double patenting, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any presented claims are rejectable, they should be rejected. If the ground of rejection would also apply to the corresponding claims in the patent, any Office action including the rejection must have the approval of the Technology Center Director. See MPEP § 1003. Interference and derivation proceedings are addressed in MPEP Chapter 2300 and 37 CFR Parts 41 and 42.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection: when proper and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination the rejection or other action may be made final; in making such final rejection the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable and clearly state the reasons in support thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim. Before final rejection a clear issue should be developed between examiner and applicant. Examiners should thoroughly search and fully apply references in the first action to bring prosecution to speedy conclusion and to avoid piecemeal examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding wholesale change in approach between examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned to act on an application which has received one or more actions by another examiner, the examiner should review the previous search to ensure it is thorough and complete and should not take an entirely new approach or attempt to reorient the point of view of a previous examiner or make a new search in the mere hope of finding something.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guidance is intended to promote continuity and fairness in prosecution; see MPEP § 904.02 for review of previous searches.
